what: The section’s bottom edge is torn into a noisy mountain ridge, and the section right below (a photo panel layered on top) shows through the gap — in the first 1.5s it rises from under the content so a ridge shows at about the bottom 10% of the first screen, from the moment the next section’s top edge touches the bottom of the screen it is tied to scroll and eats in to about 60% of the height. The ridge rises .13 more at the center (a hollow), with wobble .13 · grain 230px, slowly writhing like breathing at .15 turns per second, and surging more when scrolled fast
ease: none (tied to scroll) · initial rise smootherstep 1.5s

options.peek: Initial revealed share (ratio of section height), default .19
options.reach: Portion consumed at scroll end, default .4
options.intro: Initial surge duration (s), default 1.5 — 0 means immediate
options.agitate: Multiplier for extra wobble on fast scroll, default 2.2
options.[data-fx-part=content]: (If present) content box to measure height — if none, the whole element

use: Hero
note: Overlaps the next sibling element upward with a negative margin-top and adds extra height (padding-bottom) beneath this element — undone when removed. The original is a contour (marching squares) of a 2D noise field, so small islands can break off above the ridge and the cursor bites into the ridge — this part has a single ridge line only (no islands, no cursor bite).

from.where: detail.js torn boundary (.d-hero → .d-trailer) — original main.js data-dissolve R{reach .4·peek .19·wander .13·intro 1.5·center .13·edge .5·life .85·lifeSpeed .15·surge .55·finish .85·scale 230·warp 1.25}
